Subject: Procurement commitment path: timeline, owners, and agreed next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested mutual action plan so we have a single source of truth for internal review at Nova: 

High-level ask from Nova: fast pilot to validate latency/cost; enterprise contract for production with PO. Current open decisions: preferred payment instrument (PO vs corporate card for pilot), interest in AWS Marketplace procurement, and timing for security evidence (SOC2/ISO reports).

Draft mutual action plan (attached: MAP_draft_NovaLabs.pdf):
- Legal review (redlines + SOW): Owner = Procurement (Nova) + Redwood Legal (Marissa) — target start: 2027-05-24, target complete: 2027-05-31
- Security review (security questionnaire & SOC2 evidence): Owner = Nova Security + Redwood Security (Ben) — target start: 2027-05-24, target complete: 2027-06-07
- Finance & PO decision: Owner = Nova Finance + Procurement — target complete: 2027-06-10
- Pilot provisioning & billing instrument: Owner = Redwood Onboarding (Karthik) + Nova IT — provisioning within 48 hours of pilot approval
- PO issuance (enterprise): Owner = Nova Finance — target issuance: within 5 business days after sign-off

Estimated end-to-end (legal -> security -> finance -> PO): ~3-4 weeks from start if reviews run in parallel. If you pursue AWS Marketplace the legal/finance path may extend by 2–3 weeks due to marketplace enrollment steps.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm whether Nova wants initial pilot on corporate card or to initiate a PO straight away.
2) Confirm interest in AWS Marketplace option (we can run parallel path but want to know whether to prioritize marketplace enrollment).
3) Confirm a day/time for a short 30-min sync next Friday (2027-05-28) to lock owners and milestones.

Attachments: MAP_draft_NovaLabs.pdf, Redwood_SOW_stub.pdf

If helpful, Ben can share the security evidence packet and a short checklist that speeds the security review.

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,

Alex — looping in some pragmatic notes from the security + procurement perspective to help you decide marketplace vs PO for initial pilot.

Short answers:
- Marketplace (AWS Marketplace): + simpler consolidated billing for infra spend, potential for faster procurement for some enterprise customers; - adds an enrollment step (seller onboarding) and contract alignment that typically adds 10–15 business days.
- Direct PO path: + fastest for customers who already have an established vendor PO process — legal review and SOW often determine cadence; - PO requires your finance team to sign and issue (we can accept the PO upon contract sign).

Suggested hybrid approach for speed: pilot on corporate card (2–3 days to provision), while beginning legal + security exchanges for the enterprise PO in parallel. That way you avoid blocking technical validation and we keep the enterprise path moving.

Rough timeline we see when tasks run in parallel (business days):
- Legal review & redlines: 5–7 BD (owner: Marissa / Nova Legal)
- Security questionnaire & evidence review (SOC2): 7–10 BD (owner: Ben / Nova Sec)
- Finance approval & PO issuance: 3–5 BD after legal sign-off (owner: Nova Finance)
- Total from start to PO in-hand (parallel run): ~2.5–3 weeks

I attached a short quickguide that outlines vendor path options (procurement-paths-quickguide.pdf) and a checklist that your procurement team can use to accelerate approvals. If you want, I can jump on the security call next Wed (2027-05-26) at 10:00 PT to walk through the SOC2 artifacts with your team.

Action items:
- Alex / Procurement: confirm pilot card ok (Alex) — due EOD 2027-05-23
- Nova Security: confirm availability for a security call (Ben to join) — due 2027-05-25
- Redwood Legal (Marissa): draft SOW redline ready for first pass by 2027-05-25

Cheers,
